syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Kaveri
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

chapters.title: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read

topics.title: Village life, Triveni and the serial Kashi Yatre

concepts.learning_objective: Students will describe the north Karnataka village setting and why news and magazines arrived late.
Students will explain the plot of Triveni's Kashi Yatre and why the grandmother identified with its protagonist.

topics.title: The narrator's absence and the grandmother's past

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain why the grandmother's tears surprised and worried the narrator.
Students will relate the grandmother's childhood and lack of schooling to her regret.

topics.title: The resolve to learn and the tuition

concepts.learning_objective: Students will interpret the grandmother's feeling of dependence and her wish to be independent.
Students will evaluate the grandmother's belief that there is no age bar for learning.
Students will describe how the grandmother worked as a learner.

topics.title: Dassara, the gift and respect for a teacher

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain why the grandmother touched the narrator's feet on Saraswati Puja day.
Students will identify the story's message about education, independence and lifelong learning.

topics.title: Binomials, prefixes and idioms of learning
topics.ncert_sections: Vocabulary and Structures in Context I-IV

concepts.learning_objective: Students will identify binomials and use them correctly in context.
Students will form opposite words with the prefixes un-, in-, im-, dis- and mis-.
Students will match idioms related to learning with their meanings.

topics.title: Simple past and past perfect tense
topics.ncert_sections: Vocabulary and Structures in Context V

concepts.learning_objective: Students will recognise the form of the past perfect tense (had + past participle).
Students will use the past perfect for the earlier of two completed past actions.

topics.title: The poem Bharat Our Land

concepts.learning_objective: Students will interpret the images and symbols the poet uses to praise India.
Students will identify the refrain, hyperbole, allusion and ode form in the poem.

topics.title: Sentila's dream and Arenla's objection

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Sentila secretly pursued her dream of becoming a pot maker.
Identify the hardships and poor returns that made Arenla prefer weaving for her daughter.

topics.title: Watching the potters and the village council

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the stages of pot making that Sentila watched, from pounding the clay to firing the kiln.
Interpret the council's view that traditional skills belong to the community and must be passed on.

topics.title: Learning from Arenla and Onula

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how Sentila's year of training with her mother left her frustrated.
Analyse how Onula's calm guidance and advice to observe helped Sentila gain confidence.

topics.title: A new pot maker is born

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Sentila suddenly matched her mother's speed and skill on the last day.
Evaluate the meaning of the two identical rows of pots and the line 'A new pot maker was born'.

topics.title: Vocabulary and structures in context

concepts.learning_objective: Use the meanings of words from the story and classify pot making words as tools, materials and processes.
Identify noun clauses and relative (adjectival) clauses in sentences from the story.
Identify determiners and the information they give about a noun.

topics.title: Gifts of Grace: Honouring Our Vocations

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the poem celebrates the varied vocations of Bharat and the identity they give to workers.
Identify the form, tone and poetic devices used in the poem.

topics.title: Origin and early history of the pankha

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the origin of the words pankha and pankhi and the early evidence of their use.
Describe how pankhas were used and valued in ancient India.

topics.title: Pankhas of Rajasthan and Gujarat

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the applique, zardozi, temple and painted hand fans of Rajasthan.
Identify the mirror-work, bead and Kutch leather hand fans of Gujarat.

topics.title: Pankhas of Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, Bihar and the tribes

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the sola, palm leaf, Phadh and bamboo fans of other states.
Describe the materials and designs of tribal hand fans.

topics.title: Changing role and preservation of the pankha

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how technology and commerce have changed the role of the pankha.
Evaluate the ways suggested for preserving the pankha craft.
Interpret the significance of the title 'Winds of Change'.

topics.title: Vocabulary and structures: word pairs, collocations and the present perfect

concepts.learning_objective: Classify word pairs and use fixed expressions with 'and' correctly.
Choose conventional word combinations (collocations) in context.
Use the present perfect tense for past actions relevant to the present.

topics.title: The Last Leaf (O. Henry)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Johnsy's illness, her despair and her recovery.
Interpret Behrman's sacrifice and the meaning of his masterpiece.

topics.title: Canvas of Soil: the garden as a painting

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the poet's comparison of a garden with a painting.
Identify and interpret metaphor and imagery in the poem.

topics.title: Canvas of Soil: poetic devices and allegory

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the rhyme scheme, alliteration and tone of the poem.
Interpret the poem as an allegory with surface and deeper meanings.

topics.title: Reading for Meaning I: Grandpa comes to live in the city

concepts.learning_objective: The learner recalls why Grandpa moved to the city, his past life and his feelings about it.
The learner explains Ravi's reactions to his mother's instructions and the dilemma they create.

topics.title: Reading for Meaning II: Grandpa's day out

concepts.learning_objective: The learner sequences and interprets the stops Grandpa makes on his day out.
The learner evaluates how successfully Ravi trails Grandpa and how he is fooled.

topics.title: Reading for Meaning III: The birthday surprise

concepts.learning_objective: The learner explains Grandpa's birthday tradition and the reactions it produces.
The learner infers that Grandpa knew Ravi had been following him.
The learner evaluates the irony of the title by judging whose memory actually fails.

topics.title: Vocabulary and Structures in Context

concepts.learning_objective: The learner identifies meanings of words from the story and classifies movement and sound words.
The learner uses prepositions of place and direction correctly.
The learner converts Wh- and Yes/No questions into reported speech.

topics.title: Poem: I Cannot Remember My Mother

concepts.learning_objective: The learner interprets how sounds, scents and sights bring back the poet's memory of his mother.
The learner identifies the poet and the purpose of the refrain.

topics.title: Speaking and sensory words: intonation and senses

concepts.learning_objective: The learner chooses the intonation that suits Wh-, Yes/No and choice questions.
The learner classifies words as visual, auditory, olfactory or tactile.

topics.title: Paralympics and Dr Deepa Malik's turning point
topics.ncert_sections: Paralympics: Reading for Meaning (introduction, start of the interview)

concepts.learning_objective: The learner identifies what the Paralympic Games celebrate and India's early Paralympic history.
The learner explains how Dr Deepa Malik turned a life-changing illness into a new beginning in para-athletics.

topics.title: Achievements, challenges and advocacy
topics.ncert_sections: Paralympics: Reading for Meaning (rest of the interview)

concepts.learning_objective: The learner recalls Dr Malik's 'firsts' and interprets her belief in 'ability beyond disability'.
The learner explains how Dr Malik and the Paralympics challenge stereotypes about disability.
The learner describes Dr Malik's advocacy work and her vision of an inclusive society.

topics.title: Fact and opinion, cause and effect, and phrases in context
topics.ncert_sections: Paralympics: Check Your Understanding; Vocabulary I

concepts.learning_objective: The learner distinguishes verifiable facts from personal opinions in the interview.
The learner identifies cause-effect relationships between events in the text.
The learner interprets phrases such as 'in hindsight' and 'defy the odds' in context.

topics.title: Modal auxiliaries and reported speech
topics.ncert_sections: Paralympics: Vocabulary and Structures in Context III-VI

concepts.learning_objective: The learner identifies the function of modal verbs such as could, should and would in sentences.
The learner converts direct speech into reported speech, making the required changes.

topics.title: Nine Gold Medals: the story and its message
topics.ncert_sections: Nine Gold Medals: poem, Check Your Understanding, Critical Reflection

concepts.learning_objective: The learner recalls and interprets the sequence of events in the race described in the poem.
The learner analyses the poem's message of empathy, togetherness and inclusion.

topics.title: Poetic devices, collocations and the Olympic movements
topics.ncert_sections: Nine Gold Medals: appreciation, Vocabulary in Context; Learning Beyond the Text

concepts.learning_objective: The learner identifies alliteration and imagery in the poem and knows its poet.
The learner recognises natural adjective-noun collocations.
The learner distinguishes the Olympics, Paralympics and Special Olympics from the information given.

topics.title: Act I: The rehearsal and Shruti's dilemma

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the setting of Act I and the members of the fusion group with their instruments.
Explain why Shruti hesitates to tell her father about the fusion concert and how her friends encourage her.

topics.title: Act II: The conversation at dinner

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Nabin's reasons for refusing Shruti permission to join the fusion concert.
Interpret Leela's reaction to Shruti's secret rehearsals.

topics.title: Act III: The rehearsal, Nabin's past and reconciliation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Shruti's parents respond to the group's rehearsal.
Explain how Leela's account of Nabin's own past changes his attitude.

topics.title: Themes, title and characters of the play

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how the play explores the meeting of tradition and modernity and justify its title.
Evaluate how Nabin's attitude towards music evolves through the play.

topics.title: Writing a play script: aside, stage directions and fillers
topics.ncert_sections: Vocabulary and Structures in Context I-II; Writing Task; Learning Beyond the Text I

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the use of an aside, brackets, colons and ellipsis in a play script.
Recognise non-lexical fillers and the purpose they serve in speech.

topics.title: Vocabulary and reported speech
topics.ncert_sections: Vocabulary and Structures in Context III-VII

concepts.learning_objective: Use the idioms and music-related words of the play in context.
Convert exclamatory sentences into declarative sentences in reported speech.

topics.title: Poem: A Friend Found in Music
topics.ncert_sections: A Friend Found in Music; Vocabulary in Context

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the metaphors, mood and message of the poem.
Explain the meaning of phrasal verbs such as 'pull through' and 'move on'.

topics.title: Khetaram, the Gramin Dak Sewak of the Thar
topics.ncert_sections: Carrier of Words, Part I (Khetaram's daily work in the desert)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall who Khetaram is and describe the remote area he serves near the Indo-Pakistan border.
Explain the physical hardships Khetaram faces while delivering mail in the Thar desert.

topics.title: Gramin Dak Sewaks and the mission of India Post
topics.ncert_sections: Carrier of Words, Part I (GDS across India; India Post after independence)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe who Gramin Dak Sewaks are and why their role in remote areas is invaluable.
Distinguish the purpose of India Post after independence from that of the British postal system.

topics.title: Livelihood, trust and the money order
topics.ncert_sections: Carrier of Words, Part II (GDS service conditions; money orders; trust of villagers)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the conditions of GDS service and why they help retain a large rural workforce.
Interpret instances from the text that show villagers' trust in the post office and the GDS.

topics.title: Khetaram's character and the bearer of news
topics.ncert_sections: Carrier of Words, Part II (letters of joy and grief; waiting for phone lines)

concepts.learning_objective: Infer Khetaram's beliefs and temperament from his handling of good and bad news and his hopes for the future.

topics.title: Language in context: vocabulary and structures
topics.ncert_sections: Vocabulary and Structures in Context (phrases, alliteration and metaphor, present perfect tense, active and passive voice)

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret phrases and identify alliteration and metaphor used in the chapter.
Use the present perfect tense (has/have + past participle) correctly in context.
Change sentences from active to passive voice based on the chapter's examples.

topics.title: Words by Charles Swain: meaning and theme

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the poet's view that a few sincere words are worth more than many empty ones.
Interpret the meaning of individual stanzas and images in the poem.

topics.title: Words: poetic devices and form
topics.ncert_sections: Let us appreciate the poem (rhyme scheme, simile, metaphor, hyperbole, repetition)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify simile, metaphor and hyperbole in the poem and explain their effect.
Identify the rhyme scheme and rhythm of the poem.

topics.title: The letter: passion, effort and sacrifice

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the stages the mother describes, from passion and conviction to plunging into a dream.
Explain why the mother asks Ming to count the cost of a dream in effort, money and sacrifice.

topics.title: Support, obstacles and changing dreams

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how the Academy Awards example shows the role of a support network.
Identify the reasons the mother gives for dreams remaining unfulfilled.
Interpret the mother's view that life may change a person's dreams.

topics.title: Vocabulary in context: -scape words and idioms
topics.ncert_sections: Vocabulary and Structures in Context I-II

concepts.learning_objective: Use compound words ending in '-scape' correctly in context.
Interpret idiomatic expressions from the letter such as 'wet blanket' and 'buoyed up'.

topics.title: Grammar: conditionals with imperatives and uses of 'could'
topics.ncert_sections: Vocabulary and Structures in Context III-V

concepts.learning_objective: Form first conditional sentences with an imperative in the main clause.
Distinguish the functions of 'could' such as possibility, past ability, purpose and hypothesis.

topics.title: The poem 'Step up to the challenge': theme, tone and form
topics.ncert_sections: Believe in Yourself: Reading for Appreciation; Check your Understanding

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the central idea of each stanza of the poem.
Identify the rhyme scheme, tone and poet of the poem.

topics.title: Poetic devices and Latin expressions
topics.ncert_sections: Believe in Yourself: Check your Understanding VI-VIII; Vocabulary in Context

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the metaphor and antithesis used in the poem.
Explain the purpose of a rhetorical question in the poem.
Use Latin expressions such as 'status quo' and 'ad hoc' correctly.
